parsed_answer.content:
In Spring Boot, a test slice is a specialized testing mechanism designed to load only a curated, domain-specific subset of the application context instead of spinning up the entire heavy-duty root ApplicationContext via @SpringBootTest. When writing integration tests for large enterprise systems, loading every single bean, configuration class, and third-party starter can degrade test execution speed and bloat memory overhead. Test slices solve this by leveraging meta-annotations annotated with @BootstrapWith and @ImportAutoConfiguration, which selectively filter the auto-configuration classes and candidate components registered in the BeanFactory.

At the core of test slices are specialized annotations like @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, @JsonTest, and @RestClientTest. Each slice targets a distinct architectural tier. For example, @WebMvcTest restricts the classpath scan to Spring MVC controllers, controller advice, filters, and WebMvcConfigurer beans, entirely omitting persistence layers, service beans, and security chains unless explicitly mocked or imported. Similarly, @DataJpaTest configures an embedded database, registers Hibernate and Spring Data repositories, and disables full-context component scanning, giving developers a rapid feedback loop for data access logic without touching external infrastructure.

items: Test slices dynamically modify the BeanFactory PostProcessor phase by scanning only for specific marker annotations or filtering out irrelevant auto-configuration candidates via exclusion filters defined in META-INF/spring.factories or spring/autoconfigure.imports.

They automatically configure an embedded database (like H2 or HSQLDB) for persistence slices unless overridden, and wrap database interactions in a transaction by default, rolling back changes after each test method execution.

They provide dedicated test-scoped infrastructure beans (such as MockMvc for web slices or TestEntityManager for JPA slices) pre-injected into the test class, removing the need for manual setup boilerplate.

parsed_answer.content: A common production gotcha with test slices is mistakenly injecting beans that belong to an excluded layer. For instance, using @WebMvcTest means your @Service and @Repository beans are NOT loaded into the ApplicationContext; attempting to @Autowired them directly will cause a NoSuchBeanDefinitionException unless you use @MockBean to supply a mock substitute, or explicitly use @Import to pull in the specific service class.
